summary:
Zootoca vivipara, the common or viviparous lizard, is a small terrestrial lizard with the widest range of any lizard, extending across northern Eurasia into subarctic regions. It is Ireland’s only native terrestrial reptile. It lives in heathland, moorland, woodland and grassland, hibernates from October to March, and eats insects and spiders. It thermoregulates by basking even in cold climates and can survive freezing; groundwater-warmed soil provides refuges.

Most populations give birth to live young, while egg-laying populations occur in northern Spain and southwestern France. The evolution of these reproductive modes is debated, with research indicating multiple origins of live birth and reversals to egg-laying. Lizards reach sexual maturity in their second year and typically live five to six years.

Adults average 50–77 mm long. Males are generally brighter and have larger heads, which are associated with greater mating and combat success. Females have inherited yellow, orange or mixed color morphs linked to reproductive differences; each has distinct fitness advantages.
